lines.text: That voice you hate on recordings? That's the one everyone else hears!
When you talk, sound reaches your ears two different ways.
First, through the air, just like everyone else hears you.
Second, straight through your skull bones, to your inner ear.
And bones boost the deep, low tones, so your own voice sounds rich and full.
But a microphone only catches the air route.
No bone bass, so the recording sounds thinner and higher.
So is the recording wrong? Nope!
It's actually how everyone else hears you every day.
You're the only person who never hears your real voice. Wild, right?
